policy_name: Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of AI and Autonomy
question: The document defines autonomy as a 'spectrum'; how do the proposed measures for responsible development, deployment, and use account for the varying degrees of autonomy within military AI capabilities?
answer_low_temp:
The proposed measures for responsible development, deployment, and use of military AI capabilities, including those enabling autonomous functions and systems, account for the varying degrees of autonomy within these systems by emphasizing the need for transparency, audibility, and appropriate training of personnel.

For instance, the measure that states military AI capabilities should be developed with methodologies, data sources, design procedures, and documentation that are transparent to and auditable by relevant defense personnel (point 7) applies to all levels of autonomy. This ensures that personnel can understand the workings of the system, regardless of its level of autonomy, to make informed decisions about its use.

Similarly, the measure that personnel who use or approve the use of military AI capabilities should be trained to understand the capabilities and limitations of those systems (point 8) applies to all levels of autonomy. This training equips personnel to make appropriate context-informed judgments on the use of AI systems, regardless of their level of autonomy.

Moreover, the measure that military AI capabilities should have explicit, well-defined uses and be designed and engineered to fulfill those intended functions (point 9) also applies to all levels of autonomy. This ensures that the system's purpose and limitations are clearly defined, regardless of its level of autonomy.

Lastly, the measure that states should implement appropriate safeguards to mitigate risks of failures in military AI capabilities, such as the ability to detect and avoid unintended consequences and the ability to respond, for example by disengaging or deactivating deployed systems, when such systems demonstrate unintended behavior (point 10) applies to all levels of autonomy. This measure ensures that systems can be controlled and stopped if they demonstrate unintended behavior, regardless of their level of autonomy.

In summary, the proposed measures for responsible development, deployment, and use of military AI capabilities, including those enabling autonomous functions and systems, account for the varying degrees of autonomy within these systems by emphasizing transparency, audibility, appropriate training, well-defined uses, and the implementation of appropriate safeguards.

Citation: The Tallinn Manual 2.0 on the International Law Applicable to Cyber Operations (2017), Cambridge University Press.

Document ID: https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/monkey-cage/wp/2019/0

answer_high_temp: The Export Enforcement Coordination Center, established by S. 4085, will coordinate export enforcement among various executive departments and agencies (Section 2(b)). Its primary functions include serving as a forum for enhancing and coordinating export control efforts, resolving conflicts in investigations, exchanging information related to potential violations of export controls, serving as a primary point of contact between enforcement authorities and agencies engaged in export licensing, coordinating law enforcement public outreach activities, and establishing governmentwide statistical tracking capabilities (Section 2(c)). The Center will be directed by a full-time senior officer or employee of the Department of Homeland Security, with deputy directors from the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice, and an Intelligence Community Liaison (Section 2(d)). The Center will interact with the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, the Department of Defense, the Department of Justice, the Department of Commerce, the Department of Energy, the Department of Homeland Security, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and such other executive branch departments, agencies, or offices as the President may designate (Section 2(b)).

question: What constitutes 'sensitive technologies' according to Section 3 of the Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024, particularly in relation to artificial intelligence and quantum technology?
answer_low_temp: According to Section 3 of the Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024,'sensitive technologies' include technologies relating to semiconductors, the development of advanced artificial intelligence capabilities, and the development of quantum technology components and capabilities (Sec. 3(b)(1)(A-C)). The Act does not provide a specific definition of these technologies, so the interpretation of what constitutes 'advanced artificial intelligence capabilities' and 'quantum technology components and capabilities' may vary. For more detailed information on these technologies, refer to relevant sources such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) for quantum technology (https://www.nist.gov/quantum-technology) and the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource Task Force report for artificial intelligence (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/AI-Roadmap-Final-Report.pdf).
